_comment: Artifacts in this release directory whose provenance is NOT resolved, recorded 2026-09-09.
These files are deliberately kept on disk and deliberately excluded from every automatic
rescue-package selection. They are not deleted, because a file whose history is unclear is
still evidence; they are not silently re-recorded at their current hash, because doing that
converts an open question into a false assurance -- which is how this directory reached the
state below in the first place.
HOW THIS WAS FOUND. scripts/verify_msv3_release_archive.py compared the bytes on disk
against the two tracked integrity records in this directory. SHA256SUMS.txt and
release-manifest.json disagreed with the bytes AND with each other. The signed-ota packages
below still carry valid signatures and correct embedded identities, so nothing here is
forged; what is lost is the guarantee that a (name, application_version) pair names exactly
one image forever. Each of these was rebuilt under a name and version already in use.
NONE OF THESE IS A RESCUE PACKAGE FOR A PROBE ABOUT TO BE COATED. Probes 5, 6, 7 and 8 run
bootloader 1.0.3 and their rescue packages live in ../1.0.3/, which is clean. Probe 4's
running image already has a separate, documented provenance gap recorded in MSV3/fleet.json,
and its fleet entry pins installed_application_version to 0.
TO RESOLVE AN ENTRY: rebuild it from a clean checkout at the recorded commit and compare
bytes, or supersede it with a NEW application version and delete the ambiguous one. Do not
resolve an entry by editing a hash.

disputed.name: msv3-1.0.2-sensor004-initial-install-from-stock.zip
disputed.reason: SHA256SUMS.txt and release-manifest.json record different hashes for this name; the manifest was updated to the current bytes and the checksum file was not.

disputed.name: msv3-1.0.2-sensor004-v65550-signed-ota.zip
disputed.reason: Same application version 65550 now denotes different bytes. The image on disk is signed, sensor 004, build 2026-09-06-s4v50, 132448 bytes. Whether the superseded bytes were ever transferred to probe 4 is not recorded anywhere.

disputed.name: msv3-1.0.2-sensor099-initial-install-from-stock.zip
disputed.reason: Bytes differ from SHA256SUMS.txt and the file grew from 324081 to 328969 bytes, so this 1.0.2-named bundle does not contain what the original 1.0.2 bundle contained. Sensor 099 no longer exists in MSV3/fleet.json; that identity was reassigned to probe 8 on 2026-09-08.

disputed.name: msv3-1.0.2-sensor099-v65549-signed-ota.zip
disputed.reason: Rebuilt under an existing name and version. Sensor 099 is no longer a fleet identity.

disputed.name: msv3-1.0.2-sensor099-v65550-signed-ota.zip
disputed.reason: Rebuilt under an existing name and version. Sensor 099 is no longer a fleet identity.

disputed.name: msv3-1.0.2-sensor099-v65551-signed-ota.zip
disputed.reason: Listed in SHA256SUMS.txt but no longer on disk. The similarly-versioned file that remains, HANGTEST-msv3-1.0.2-sensor099-v65551-signed-ota.zip, is NOT the same bytes, so this was a rebuild-and-rename rather than a rename.

disputed.name: HANGTEST-msv3-1.0.2-sensor099-v65551-signed-ota.zip
disputed.reason: This is the dead-stripped hang-test image described in MSV3_Moisture_BLE_Sleep.ino: because the deliberate hang made the advertising path unreachable, the linker discarded it and the MSV3-MOISTURE-NNN literal with it. The image is 93360 bytes instead of the normal ~132448 and carries NO MSV3-BUILD id at all. It is validly signed and still matches an identity regex, which is exactly why it must never be reachable by a rescue flow.
disputed.embedded_identity: sensor 099, application_version 65551, NO build id, signed, 93360-byte image
